'''William Toby White''' is an Australian [[ichthyology|ichthyologist]]. He studies [[speciation]] and [[biodiversity]] of [[shark]], [[Batoidea|ray]], and [[Skate (fish)|skate]] species (subclass [[Elasmobranchii]]) through morphological and molecular [[systematics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://people.csiro.au/W/W/William-White.aspx|title=Dr Will White}}</ref>

== Education ==
White received bachelor's (1997) and doctoral (2003) degrees in Biological Science from [[Murdoch University]] in [[Perth]], [[Australia]]. His doctoral thesis, "Aspects of the biology of elasmobranchs in a subtropical embayment in Western Australia and of chondrichthyan fisheries in Indonesia", examined 1) spatial partitioning of food resources available to shark, ray, and skate species in Shark Bay (off the western coast of Australia), and 2) the relative frequencies of shark, ray, and skate species caught in fisheries off the coast of southeastern Indonesia.<ref>{{Cite thesis|url=http://researchrepository.murdoch.edu.au/402/|title=Aspects of the biology of elasmobranchs in a subtropical embayment in Western Australia and of chondrichthyan fisheries in Indonesia|year=2003|publisher=Murdoch University|type=phd|last1=White|first1=William Toby}}</ref> From 2004 to 2006 he did post-doctoral training, also at Murdoch University.

== Professional career ==
Since 2006, White has served as ichthyologist at the Australian National Fish Collection which is part of the [[CSIRO]] Marine and Atmospheric Research facility in [[Hobart]], the capital of the Australian state of [[Tasmania]]. {{Asof|2014}}, he has at least 137 publications, which have been cited at least 1767 times.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=ImtgN4cAAAAJ&hl=en|title = William White|access-date = 2014-12-06|website = Google Scholars}}</ref> He has described over 50 new sharks and rays, as well as 7 new bony fishes ([[Teleostei|teleosts]]) in publications which he authored or co-authored,<ref name="ResearchGate">{{ResearchGate|William_White7}}</ref> including the discovery and naming of the shark species ''[[Squalus formosus]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2011/09/110901-shark-new-species-eaten-science-ocean-squalus-formosus-dogfish/|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110928001127/http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2011/09/110901-shark-new-species-eaten-science-ocean-squalus-formosus-dogfish|url-status = dead|archive-date = 28 September 2011|title = New Shark Species Found in Food Market|date = 1 September 2011|access-date = 6 December 2014|website = National Geographic|last = Roach|first = John}}</ref> Another stated area of research interest is fishery management of developing countries, particularly in Papua New Guinea and the Indonesian archipelago.<ref name="ResearchGate" /> Since 2011, he has served as editor for the journal ''Ichthyological Research''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.springer.com/life+sciences/animal+sciences/journal/10228?detailsPage=editorialBoard|title = Ichthyological Research}}</ref>
